cover.headline: 5 hook formulas that work in any niche.
cover.subheadline: Steal these for your next 5 videos.

slides.title: "I tried / quit / lost..."
slides.body: Personal stakes. People stay to see what happened.

slides.title: "Most people don't know..."
slides.body: A curiosity gap. Implies you have the inside answer.

slides.title: "If you're [X], stop doing [Y]."
slides.body: Calls out a specific person. They can't scroll past themselves.

slides.title: "Here's the truth about [X]."
slides.body: Positions you as the one cutting through the noise.

slides.title: "[Number] things I learned about [X]."
slides.body: Promises a list. The brain wants to finish what it starts.

caption:
5 hook formulas that work in any niche:

1. "I tried / quit / lost..."
2. "Most people don't know..."
3. "If you're [X], stop doing [Y]."
4. "Here's the truth about [X]."
5. "[Number] things I learned about [X]."

cover.headline: 7 things to check before every shoot.
cover.subheadline: Number 4 is the one everyone skips.

slides.title: 1. 4K at 60fps
slides.body: The only camera setting that really matters. Set it once.

slides.title: 2. Mic test and playback
slides.body: Record 5 seconds and listen back. Don't trust the meter alone.

slides.title: 3. Hook pre-written
slides.body: 1.5 seconds, memorized. Never improvise the first line.

slides.title: 4. Scout your spots
slides.body: Switch location every line. This is the one people skip.

slides.title: 5. Batteries and storage
slides.body: Two of everything. A dead battery ends the day.

slides.title: 6. Backup device
slides.body: One failure shouldn't cancel the whole shoot.

slides.title: 7. Frame for the title
slides.body: Leave headroom so the overlay never covers your face.

caption:
Run this before every shoot. Number 4 is why most talking-head videos feel flat.

slides.title: 1. Too small
slides.body: If it's hard to read on a phone, it's costing you watch time.

slides.title: 2. Off the beat
slides.body: Text should hit on the cut, not lag behind the sentence.

slides.title: 3. Buried at the bottom
slides.body: The app UI covers it. Keep key words in the safe zone.

slides.title: 4. Wrong font
slides.body: White, modern, sans-serif. No heavy drop shadow.

slides.title: 5. Paced too slow
slides.body: Captions should feel a touch faster than the video itself.

caption:
Captions aren't decoration, they're a retention tool. These 5 mistakes quietly leak your views:

1. Too small
2. Off the beat
3. Buried at the bottom
4. Wrong font

slides.title: Act 1 — Hook (0 to 1.5s)
slides.body: State the problem sharp. No intro, no setup. Stop the thumb.

slides.title: Act 2 — Tension (4 to 12s)
slides.body: Build the gap. Give a reason to keep watching past second 4.

slides.title: Act 3 — Payoff (13s to end)
slides.body: Deliver the answer, then one clean close. Don't trail off.

slides.title: Why most fail
slides.body: They film all hook or all payoff. The tension in the middle is what holds people.

caption:
Every short-form video that pops has 3 acts. Most people film one and wonder why retention dies.

Hook (0 to 1.5s)
Tension (4 to 12s)
Payoff (13s+)

cover.headline: 5 ways to fix your retention curve.

slides.title: 1. Open on motion
slides.body: A static first frame loses people before you speak.

slides.title: 2. Patch second 4
slides.body: Drop a number or contradiction right where attention dips.

slides.title: 3. Cut the dead air
slides.body: Remove the breath before every sentence. Pace is retention.

slides.title: 4. Switch the frame
slides.body: New angle or location keeps the eye from settling.

slides.title: 5. Pay off the hook
slides.body: Deliver what you promised before they lose patience.

caption:
Retention isn't luck, it's a series of small saves.

1. Open on motion
2. Patch second 4
3. Cut the dead air
4. Switch the frame
5. Pay off the hook

cover.headline: 5 rules for B-roll that isn't boring.
cover.subheadline: Most people film the wrong thing.

slides.title: 1. Film nouns, not verbs
slides.body: The object close-up beats the wide action shot.

slides.title: 2. Get uncomfortably close
slides.body: Detail reads as intentional. Distance reads as filler.

slides.title: 3. Move the camera
slides.body: A slow push or pan adds life a locked shot can't.

slides.title: 4. Match the light
slides.body: Consistent lighting makes cuts feel seamless.

slides.title: 5. Overshoot
slides.body: Capture 3x what you need. You'll thank yourself in the edit.

caption:
Boring B-roll is usually the wrong subject filmed from too far.

1. Film nouns, not verbs
2. Get uncomfortably close
3. Move the camera
4. Match the light
5. Overshoot

cover.headline: 4 audio mistakes that ruin good video.
cover.subheadline: People hear bad audio before they see good video.

slides.title: 1. Music too loud
slides.body: If you notice the track, it's already drowning the voice.

slides.title: 2. No mic
slides.body: Phone audio echoes. A cheap clip mic is a night-and-day upgrade.

slides.title: 3. Inconsistent levels
slides.body: Volume jumping between clips makes it feel amateur.

slides.title: 4. Dead silence
slides.body: A subtle bed of music under the voice keeps energy up.

caption:
People forgive average video. They scroll on bad audio instantly.

1. Music too loud
2. No mic
3. Inconsistent levels
4. Dead silence

Fix the sound and watch retention rise.

cover.headline: 5 ways to edit twice as fast.

slides.title: 1. Cut on the first pass
slides.body: Make decisions as you watch. Don't re-watch endlessly.

slides.title: 2. Build a caption style
slides.body: Save your font and look once. Reuse it every time.

slides.title: 3. Keep a music folder
slides.body: Stop hunting. Pull from tracks you've already cleared.

slides.title: 4. Template your export
slides.body: Set it once: format, size, settings. Never rethink it.

slides.title: 5. Stop polishing dead air
slides.body: Cut the slow parts instead of perfecting them.

caption:
Editing slow is usually a workflow problem, not a skill problem.

1. Cut on the first pass

Speed comes from systems, not rushing.

slides.title: 1. Predict the future.
slides.body: "This is going to change how [your niche] works." Present vs. future = instant curiosity.

slides.title: 2. Show the experiment.
slides.body: "I tried [new way] for 30 days — here's what happened." A friend showing a friend.

slides.title: 3. Teach the lesson.
slides.body: "Here's how [someone] solved [pain point]." You found the answer — break it down.

slides.title: 4. Force the look.
slides.body: "Check this out." Point the eye at one thing moving on screen. Attention first, context second.

slides.title: 5. Reveal the secret.
slides.body: "Nobody talks about why [surprising thing]." The gap between what they know and what you found.

slides.title: 6. Say the unpopular thing.
slides.body: "Everyone does [X]. Everyone's wrong." State the belief, then break it.

caption:
6 ways to frame any hook — same topic, six angles:

1. Predict the future.
2. Show the experiment.
3. Teach the lesson.
4. Force the look.
5. Reveal the secret.
6. Say the unpopular thing.

Stuck on a hook? Run your topic through all six and pick the one with the most contrast.

cover.headline: Your hook died for 1 of 4 reasons.

slides.title: 1. Too slow.
slides.body: The topic isn't in your first sentence. Every second of warm-up costs you viewers. Cut everything before the point.

slides.title: 2. Too confusing.
slides.body: If a 6th grader can't repeat your first line back, rewrite it. Short words. Active voice. One meaning.

slides.title: 3. Not for them.
slides.body: "I struggled with..." makes them guess if it applies. "If YOU struggle with..." removes the guess. Name their pain.

slides.title: 4. No tension.
slides.body: Clear but boring = no contrast. Add the gap: "Most people do A — but B works 3x better." Curiosity lives in that gap.

caption:
If a video flopped, the hook failed one of these 4 checks:

1. Too slow — topic wasn't in line one.
2. Too confusing — more than one way to read it.
3. Not for them — no "you," no pain point.
4. No tension — nothing to be curious about.

Run your last flop through this list. You'll find it in 30 seconds.
